To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the PR was significantly lower 30 days PI in the first lactation heifers, 2. the LEL was significantly higher in the first lactations heifers, 3. the PR was higher when the milk protein and milk fat content were higher, 4. the PR was lower when the milk protein/fats ratio were higher and the milk production was higher.

the pregnancy rate is significantly lower 60 day within post-partum, the milk protein/fats ratio is positively correlated with early and late pregnancy rate, the milk protein and the milk fats content are negatively correlated with early and later pregnancy rate and a late stage of pregnancy (60 days PI), the milk production has an adverse effect for retaining of the pregnancy.
the pregnancy rate and late pregnancy loss are influenced by milk production and contents and by the day after calvings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that affect the PR in dairy cattle.
a better understanding of the factors influencing pregnancy rate in dairy cattle.
the influence of milk production and contents, the day of calving and the sire on the PR and LEL in dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the milk production and milk composition have a significant effect for pregnancy rate and retention of pregnancy.
milk production and milk composition have a significant influence on the early PR, but not on the LEL, and that the PR is higher on the farms where the PR is higher in the early stage.
the PR and LEL are influenced by the milk production and milk content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PR of the dairy cattle depends on the day of calving and the milk contents.
a higher milk yield, higher fat and protein ratio and a higher milk protein content are unfavourable factors for the PR.
the milk production and its composition, the stage of lactation and the AI bull can influence the PR and the late LEL in dairy cattle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PR and LEL are significantly correlated with the milk production and the milk contents.
milk production and milk content have a significant impact on the PR.
it is necessary to consider the effect of milk contents, the DAC and the sire on PR and LEL in dairy cows.
